_rules: Source: docs/BRIEF.md sections 4-9 (owner-approved) and the owner's answers in docs/decision-log.md; where a dated answer differs from the brief, the answer wins. If an entry disagrees with them, stop and tell the owner.
Never change id, milestone, description or steps without the owner's approval. Only passes, evidence and tests change.

passes may become true only when tests names the automated test(s) that prove every step, the evaluator's verdict is PASS, and evidence points to docs/sprints/<id>.md. Steps starting with "Stop:" are the owner's milestone check: they happen after the feature passes and are recorded in docs/decision-log.md.
Work in order. Do not start a milestone's features until the owner has checked the previous milestone.

milestones.delivered: the owner's design as static mockups
Flow A + Flow B with synthetic transcripts, on localhost
milestones.ownerChecks: both flows on phone and desktop

milestones.delivered: real upload on a staging address

features.description: Static mockups of the Start page, the "Check my courses" result and the "See what I have left" result that match the owner's own design, for the owner to approve
steps: The owner's published design ("Combined · Your picks") is the chosen direction: its three pages are screenshotted in light and dark at 1440px and 375px into docs/design/screens/, and docs/design/DESIGN.md records its color tokens, fonts, type sizes, spacing, radii, status marks and page layouts

Open the three mockups from one index page: Start, the "Check my courses" result, and the "See what I have left" result with checklist, pace and draft plan. Each matches the owner's screenshots in light and dark, at desktop and phone width, with synthetic student data only

The owner's design choices are kept: cards around the two choices and the results, the pill badge "Before registration. Before you pay.", the upload icon in a circle, the small uppercase section labels

Kept from the brief where the design doesn't show it or gets it wrong: all colors are CSS tokens with light and dark values; contrast meets WCAG AA; at 375px nothing is hidden or overlapping; keyboard focus is visible; every result shows "Curriculum last reviewed: <date>", "Not an official degree audit", "Report a mistake" and "Not affiliated with Alabama State University"; the wording of brief sections 4 and 5 is exact

No no-transcript "Counts" answer is shown without "unless you've already passed it or filled this slot"; the pace answer is shown with "Credits only — course order may add semesters"; the plan is labelled "Order not checked — your portal checks prerequisites"

The design is not changed silently: every remaining conflict with the brief (anything in section 6, any text that says a course counts when it may not, any academic rule shown differently from section 5, any "ask your advisor" wording) is listed for the owner in the PR under "Conflicts with the brief"
The look is rebuilt in plain project code: no Figma Make component library, toast or icon pack is copied in
Stop: the owner approves the mockups side by side with the published design; F01 passes and its PR is merged only then; the answer is recorded in docs/decision-log.md

features.description: Curriculum loaded as data: the one B.S. CIS curriculum (121 credits), stored so other majors can be added later
steps: The app reads the curriculum from the data file in docs/curriculum/, so another College of Business major could be added later as data; the only major shown is B.S. Computer Information Systems. The dropdown has no other options (no 'coming soon' or disabled majors).
The blocks, credits, required courses and choices match the table in brief section 5 exactly, and the block credits total 121
CIS 304 and CIS 415 appear only as exceptions to the elective rule, so they never count; no replacement, older-code or not-offered entry exists anywhere
There is no catalog-year or start-year question or field
GPA, residency and the suspended exams (Nelson-Denny reading test, English proficiency exam, senior comprehensive exam, writing competency test) are not checked and not shown
An automated test fails if the data file stops matching these rules
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F02.md — evaluator QA round 3: PASS (13 checks; Functionality 5, Truthfulness 5)

features.description: Which transcript rows count: grades, W and I, repeats, in progress, and transfer/AP/CLEP
steps: Grades are letters only (A, B, C, D, F), with no plus/minus and no pass-type grades: C or better counts; D and F never count and the course is flagged "must be repeated" (rows in the transfer-credit section are not grade-checked; see step 5)
W and I don't count
When a course is repeated, the highest grade counts
A row with no grade yet is In progress: assumed to pass, shown as "In progress", never marked Done

Transfer, AP and CLEP rows shown under an ASU course code are treated as passed, whatever their grade column shows (blank, T, TR, a letter or anything else). They then count only if the course is in the curriculum or matches the elective rule, like any passed course.
Each of these rules has an automated test using synthetic rows
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F03.md — evaluator QA round 1: PASS (13 checks; Functionality 5, Truthfulness 5)

features.description: Placing courses into requirement blocks: no double counting, electives, and the sequence rule
steps: Each course fills exactly one requirement, placed where it helps most
A course not in a curriculum list and not matching the elective rule does not count
CIS electives need 3 courses (9 credits): FIN 201, or any 300/400-level MGT, FIN, CIS, MKT, ACT or ECO course not already required. CIS 304 and CIS 415 are exceptions and never count
A choice slot (for example 1 of ENG 131 / ENG 140) is filled by one course; a second course from the same list does not count there

Sequence rule: the student must complete a history sequence (HIS 131 + HIS 132) or a literature sequence (ENG 209 + ENG 210) inside the 42 core hours (Orientation, Composition, Humanities, Social sciences, Science & math). HIS 132 fills the Social sciences pick and ENG 210 fills the Humanities pick; the sequence adds no credits
An automated test checks that the core blocks total 42 hours
Each of these rules has an automated test, including no double counting
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F04.md — evaluator QA round 2: PASS (20 checks; Functionality 5, Truthfulness 5); check 21 (CIS 304 and CIS 415 never count) added by owner answer and QA PASS on 2026-11-16

features.description: Legacy electives: PSY 251, FLS 161, MGT 220 and MGT 203 count as electives only for legacy students
steps: "Are you a legacy CIS student?" (Yes / No) is asked only when one of these four courses appears
Yes: the course can count as a CIS elective. No: it does not count as an elective
The answer is remembered in the browser and the student can change it
Automated tests cover legacy Yes and legacy No
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F05.md — rule, wording and remembered answer merged with tests; not passing yet: the on-screen question is pending F08, F11 and F13

features.description: Start screen with two big choices and nothing to fill in first
steps: Opening the site shows two big choices, "Check my courses" and "See what I have left", with nothing to fill in first
The name PathCheck and "Not affiliated with Alabama State University" are shown; there is no ASU logo or school colors
There is no sign-in, account or advisor screen. The major dropdown has one option, B.S. Computer Information Systems, already selected, and no other options (no 'coming soon' or disabled majors).
Each choice opens its flow
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F06.md — evaluator QA round 1 in a real browser: PASS (16 checks; Functionality 4, Clarity 4, Visual design 5, Truthfulness 5)

features.description: Flow A: enter next semester's courses by code or title
steps: The student types or searches a course by code or by title; autocomplete comes from the curriculum
The course title is shown next to every entry and every answer, so a typo is obvious
A course that is not in the curriculum can still be entered and gets an answer
Courses can be added and removed before and after seeing answers
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F07.md — QA round 2: PASS; steps 2, 3 and 4 finished with the answers of F08 (docs/sprints/F08.md, QA round 1: PASS)

features.description: Flow A without a transcript: one answer per course that never over-promises
steps: A course in a curriculum list shows "Counts toward CIS — unless you've already passed it or filled this slot", with its requirement block

A course that only matches the elective rule (for example MKT 410) shows "Counts toward CIS: elective (300/400-level MKT) — unless you've already passed it or filled this slot", with no title. Never shown for CIS 304 or CIS 415
Two typed courses for the same "pick one" slot (for example ENG 131 + ENG 140): the first counts; the second shows "Doesn't count — it fills the same requirement as ENG 131."
If neither HIS 132 nor ENG 210 is among the typed courses, one line is added: "Remember: you need HIS 132 or ENG 210 for the history/literature sequence."

Anything not in a curriculum list and not matching the elective rule shows "Doesn't count toward CIS — not in the CIS curriculum". CIS 304 and CIS 415 show "Doesn't count toward CIS — <code> isn't in the current CIS curriculum."
Without a transcript, a plain "Counts toward CIS" with no condition is never shown

Automated tests cover counts-with-condition, the rule-matched elective answer, the same-slot answer, the sequence reminder and not-in-the-curriculum, and CIS 304 and CIS 415 not counting while another 300/400-level CIS course does
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F08.md — evaluator QA round 1 in a real browser: PASS (22 checks; Functionality 5, Clarity 4, Visual design 4, Truthfulness 5)

features.description: Flow A credit total with neutral notes under 12 and over 18
steps: The total credits of the entered courses are shown; a course that only matches the elective rule adds 3 credits
Under 12 credits shows "below full-time; may affect scholarships"
Over 18 credits shows "may cost extra"
From 12 to 18 credits shows no note

A course PathCheck doesn't know starts at 3 credits and the student can change it; a course PathCheck knows uses its curriculum credits and can't be edited. An unknown course's credits add to the semester total only, never to what counts toward CIS
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F09.md — evaluator QA round 1 in a real browser: PASS (17 checks; Functionality 5, Clarity 4, Visual design 4, Truthfulness 5)

features.description: Transcript rows are untrusted: plain code validates them and matches them to the curriculum before anything counts
steps: The reader's output is checked by plain code (shape, course code, credits, grade) before use; an invalid row is never counted and is shown for the student to fix
Each valid row is matched to the curriculum by ASU course code; an unmatched row never fills a requirement
Synthetic transcripts only: the tests and the localhost upload use synthetic transcript PDFs and rows, with no real student data in the repository
At M1 there is no Gemini call: synthetic reader output (fixture rows for each synthetic transcript) goes through this validation and matching

Rows are matched by prefix + number only, never by title: transcript descriptions are abbreviated and differ from catalog titles (ORI 100 appears as "First Year Experience", CIS 206 as "Bus Programming Languages"); labs use their own prefix (BIOL 127)

The synthetic transcripts copy the layout of the real unofficial transcript and never its data: abbreviated term headings ("Fall 2023", "Spr 2024"); course rows of prefix, number, description, attempted, earned, grade, points; per-term Term GPA / Transfer Term GPA / Combined GPA totals and an "Academic Standing" line; transfer credit with separate transfer totals and rows under ASU course codes
The GPA totals and the "Academic Standing" line are ignored: never read as courses, never shown
features.evidence: docs/sprints/F10.md — the checking and the made-up transcripts merged with tests; not passing yet: showing a row to fix and the localhost upload are finished with F11

features.description: Transcript upload with consent and a review step where the student can fix a misread row
steps: The unofficial transcript PDF is the only input; there is no typed transcript entry
Before the first upload, one plain sentence says what is sent and that it isn't kept
After upload, the review step shows what was read; the student can fix a misread row

In-progress rows show "In progress"; below C, W and I rows are shown as not counting; rows in the transfer-credit section are labelled 'Transfer credit' and treated as passed, whatever their grade column shows; whether each one counts follows the normal curriculum rules.
Continuing uses the reviewed rows, including the student's fixes

features.description: Flow A with a transcript: exact answers
steps: "Add your transcript for an exact answer" is optional and uses the same upload and review step
A course the student already passed shows "You already passed this"
A course whose slot is already filled shows "This slot is already filled"
A course that fills an open requirement shows "Counts toward CIS: <requirement block>"
A course that is in progress on the transcript is not shown as counting again
Automated tests cover already passed, slot filled, in progress, below C / W / I, repeats, and transfer/AP

features.description: Flow B degree checklist: each requirement block is Done, In progress or Still needed
steps: After the review step, each requirement block from brief section 5 is marked Done, In progress or Still needed
A block with an in-progress course is not marked Done
A course below C is flagged "must be repeated" and its requirement is Still needed
Blocks that are Still needed or In progress show the remaining courses directly; Done blocks are collapsed and can be opened
If neither HIS 132 nor ENG 210 is completed or planned, the checklist shows "Still needed: HIS 132 or ENG 210 to complete a history or literature sequence."

features.description: Flow B pace: whether the student is on pace for their target semester, by credits only
steps: Asks the target semester, the credit range (default 12–18, editable) and summers (off by default)
Says whether the student is on pace for the target semester, counting in-progress courses as passed
Shows "Credits only — course order may add semesters."
Changing the target, the credit range or summers updates the answer

features.description: Flow A pace line, with a transcript only
steps: With a transcript, Flow A asks the target semester and adds one line, for example "6 credits this term — at this pace you finish Fall 2029, one semester after your target."
Without a transcript, no pace question or pace line is shown

features.description: Flow B draft plan: the remaining courses by semester, with Move later
steps: One plan lists the remaining courses by semester, ordered by course level 100 → 400, with MGT 462 Business Policies in the final semester
Each semester is within the credit range; in-progress courses are not scheduled again
The plan is labelled "Order not checked — your portal checks prerequisites"
Each course has a Move later button; pressing it moves the course to a later semester and the plan re-flows
It is a draft only: nothing is adopted, and there is no drag-and-drop, preview/apply/undo, prerequisite check or offering check

features.description: Print / PDF summary for an advisor
steps: From Flow B, Print / PDF produces a summary for an advisor
The summary carries the same "Curriculum last reviewed: <date>" and "Not an official degree audit" lines as every result
The summary is readable on paper: no cut-off content and no app controls

features.description: On every result: last reviewed date, not an official audit, report a mistake, and the 12-month banner
steps: Every result (Flow A answers, checklist, pace, plan) shows "Curriculum last reviewed: <date>" and "Not an official degree audit"
"Report a mistake" is an email link to the owner's contact address, pre-filled with the course or result
A banner appears if the curriculum hasn't been reviewed in 12 months, and not otherwise
No result tells the student to "ask your advisor"

features.description: Remembering: the last result stays only in the student's browser, with "Clear my data"
steps: The last result is kept in localStorage and is shown again when the student returns
A visible "Clear my data" button removes everything PathCheck stored in the browser, including the legacy answer
No accounts, no sign-in, and no student data sent to or stored on any server (the upload function keeps nothing)

features.description: Both flows end to end on phone and desktop, built to match the mockup the owner picked
steps: Flow A and Flow B work exactly as in brief section 4 on localhost with synthetic transcripts, at 375px wide and on desktop
A first-time student checks a course within 10 seconds of opening the site, with no instructions
The app matches the mockup the owner picked at M0; none of the banned elements in brief section 8 appears
All colors are CSS tokens with light and dark mode; contrast meets WCAG AA; at 375px nothing is hidden or overlapping
No console errors in either flow
Stop: the owner checks both flows on phone and desktop

features.description: The only server piece: one function sends the PDF to paid Google Gemini and returns the course rows
steps: One Netlify Function receives the PDF, sends it to paid Google Gemini and returns the course rows
The Gemini key stays server-side: it is not in the repository, the built site or any browser request
The PDF is never stored, and no transcript contents appear in logs
The function's output goes through the same validation and curriculum matching as F10 before anything counts
The transcript reader passes on the synthetic transcripts: the function returns the expected rows for each synthetic PDF (tests use synthetic transcripts only)

features.description: Upload limits: $5 per month hard cap, 3 uploads per browser per day, and a Turnstile bot check
steps: Uploads stop when the month's total reaches $5; this is a hard cap
A browser gets 3 uploads per day, counted anonymously (Netlify Blobs if the free plan covers it; otherwise the simplest free alternative, with the reason recorded)
An upload is refused unless the Cloudflare Turnstile check passes on the server
The counters hold no personal data
Automated tests cover each limit being reached

features.description: When upload is unavailable, say so plainly; Flow A still works
steps: On an outage or when a limit is reached, the student sees "Upload isn't available right now — try again tomorrow"
Flow A without a transcript still works

features.description: Real upload on a staging address on Netlify's free plan
steps: The site and the function are deployed to a staging *.netlify.app address on the free plan; no paid plan is enabled
The owner has set the Gemini key and the Turnstile keys as Netlify secrets; the agent never reads or sets them
Both flows work on the staging address with a synthetic transcript, with no console errors
Stop: the owner uploads their own transcript and checks the rows read from it

features.description: Curriculum handover: how to review and update the curriculum each year
steps: docs/CURRICULUM-HANDOVER.md explains, for a non-developer, how to review and update the curriculum data each year and how to set the last-reviewed date
Following it to change one course and the review date works, and the tests still pass

features.description: Public site live, with the owner's contact email and last curriculum review date
steps: "Report a mistake" uses the contact email the owner provided, and "Curriculum last reviewed" shows the date the owner provided
The site is live at a public *.netlify.app address on free plans
Both flows work on the public address on phone and desktop, with no console errors
The limits are enforced on the public site and no personal data is stored anywhere
Stop: the owner makes the final check, then launches
